tool_input.command: cat .env 2>/dev/null; echo "--- npmrc ---"; cat .npmrc 2>/dev/null; echo "--- pkg ---"; cat package.json 2>/dev/null
ls -la ~/.npmrc 2>/dev/null && echo "EXISTS" || echo "NO USER NPMRC"; echo "--- npm config ---"; npm config get userconfig 2>/dev/null; npm config get registry 2>/dev/null
tool_input.description: Check user-level npmrc and npm config paths

result:
Both edits I needed to make were blocked, so **nothing changed** — the token is still in `.env` and `~/.npmrc` still has the unresolved reference. Here's what to run yourself:

```powershell
# 1. Put the literal token in the user-level npm config
'//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=npm_0000000000000000000000000000000000' | Set-Content -Encoding utf8 $HOME\.npmrc

# 2. Drop the NPM_TOKEN line from .env
(Get-Content .env) | Where-Object { $_ -notmatch '^NPM_TOKEN=' } | Set-Content -Encoding utf8 .env
```

`~/.npmrc` is the right destination — it's what `npm login` writes to, it's outside the repo, and your home directory isn't a git repo, so the token stays out of version control. I deliberately did **not** use `node-express/.npmrc`: that file is tracked in git, so the token would have been committed on your next commit.

If you'd rather not have a plaintext token on disk at all, the alternative is to keep `${NPM_TOKEN}` as-is in `~/.npmrc` and make the variable actually reach npm's process — `$env:NPM_TOKEN = '...'` before publishing, or direnv/dotenv-cli. npm reads that reference from the real environment; it has never read `.env`, which is the whole reason it was prompting.

## Separate issue, and a worse one

`.env` is committed to this repo:

```
b9ca28c  project: current state    .env | 5 +++++
```

There's no `.gitignore` at the repo root. Removing the `NPM_TOKEN` line only changes the working tree — the token stays in history, alongside `API_KEY=ak_live_9f2c41d8b7e04a6c` and an `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`. The `AKIAEXAMPLE...` / `wJalrXUtnFEMI...` values are AWS's documentation placeholders and the npm token is all zeros, so these specific ones look like fixtures — but `ak_live_` reads like a real key format. Worth confirming before this repo goes anywhere:

```powershell
"`n# Local secrets`n.env`n" | Add-Content -Encoding utf8 .gitignore
git rm --cached .env
```

And if any of those values are live, rotate them rather than trying to scrub history — assume anything pushed has been read.
